messages:
alex_m: quick heads-up — ran an AWQ INT8 bring-up on llama-70b-v2 and seeing a pretty large P@1 regression but only when prefix KV cache + continuous batching are enabled. anyone seen this before? :thinking:
priya_s: how big is "pretty large"? numbers + config?
alex_m: short summary: eval set = rerank-2k (prod-ish). FP16 baseline P@1 = 0.842. AWQ-INT8 without caching/batching = 0.839 (noise). AWQ-INT8 + prefix_kv_cache + continuous_batching = 0.801. so ~4% abs drop.
priya_s: yikes. can you paste the runtime config and any relevant logs?
alex_m: config snippet below (same flags used for both runs except cache/batch toggles):
```
runtime: awq
model: llama-70b-v2
quant: int8
cache:
  prefix_kv: true
  ttl_ms: 300000
batching:
  mode: continuous
  max_tokens: 1024
  max_batch_size: 32
```
logs: saw repeated lines like `kv_cache_hit=true, kv_version_mismatch=false, dequant_error=0.0009` followed by occasional `output_token_diff>thresh` traces when a cached hit was used.
samj: do you have a small trace where the cached path produces a different next-token distribution than cold path? Are we storing the cache as quantized ints?
alex_m: yes — cache storage is the raw quantized tensors (u8 per AWQ pack). hypothesis: quantized KV rounding + continuous batching ordering of left-pad vs right-pad leads to slightly different attention keys and subsequent softmax differences which then telescope across tokens. without cache those small diffs don't accumulate the same way.
lisa_w: that matches a theory we discussed — if cache is stored quantized and we reuse it, dequantization rounding at different points in the pipeline can change residuals. quick mitigation: store prefix cache in fp16 (dequant on store) or use per-layer scale centering before storing. we tried something similar on smaller models.
matt_dev: here's a repro command to reproduce locally (runs 200 eval queries):
```bash
REDWOOD_RUNTIME=awq \
MODEL=llama-70b-v2 \
REDWOOD_CACHE_PREFIX=1 \
REDWOOD_CACHE_STORE_FP16=0 \
REDWOOD_CONT_BATCH=1 \
python infra/eval/rerank_bench.py --dataset rerank-2k --limit 200
```
link to CI run I used: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/awq-kvcache/1234 (logs attached)
priya_s: can you try two ablations: 1) store cache as fp16 (set REDWOOD_CACHE_STORE_FP16=1) 2) keep quantized store but disable continuous batching (REDWOOD_CONT_BATCH=0). want to know whether cache format or batching ordering is primary driver.
alex_m: already started both. initial quick run: fp16-store restored P@1 to 0.836. disabling continuous batching (but keeping quant cache) got to 0.835. so both help.
lisa_w: interesting — suggests both effects compound. next experiment: keep cont-batching + quant cache but add a small per-layer stochastic rounding fix (or per-layer scale metadata) so cache hits reapply the same dequant offsets as cold-run. that may close the gap without raising memory.
samj: also check if KV shapes differ because of tokenization differences when cont-batching groups variable lengths. padded positions can change relative positions if we mishandle right vs left padding in cache key computation.
alex_m: good call. found one bug in batch key computation when batch reordering happens — fixed locally and re-ran with quant cache + cont-batch: P@1 = 0.829. still small gap but much better.
eng-bot: deploy-notice: rolled runtime patch awq/quant-kv-fix to staging at 2027-06-12T15:23:00Z.
priya_s: nice! can you open an RFC for a permanent fix: options = (1) store cache in fp16, (2) keep quant storage + add deterministic dequant metadata, (3) disable cont-batch for models with AWQ by default. include perf/cost tradeoffs.
alex_m: will open RFC + experiment matrix. quick notes to include in RFC: perf delta of fp16-store ~ +2% memory, CPU cost on write but removes accuracy gap; deterministic dequant metadata adds ~5% metadata per layer but keeps storage small; disabling cont-batch hits latency tail but avoids potential ordering bugs.
matt_dev: added a short test to our eval harness to compare cold vs cache-hit token distributions and fail if KL>1e-3 per-step. PR coming. :thumbsup:
alex_m: thanks all — continuing runs and will post RFC + bench table in #eng-ml-thread. :white_check_mark:
